notes: Physical properties are representative ranges rather than fixed constants.
Electrical conductivity and resistivity are reciprocal properties.
Electrical properties vary strongly with porosity, pore-fluid salinity, water saturation, clay content, temperature, fractures and mineralization.
Porosity values represent typical ranges for relatively intact natural rock and can vary substantially with burial, cementation, fracturing and alteration.
Mohs hardness is approximate for rocks because rocks are aggregates of minerals rather than single minerals.
disclaimer: Conductivity and resistivity are reciprocal quantities:

The USGS describes resistivity in Ω·m and conductivity in S/m and notes that pore fluids  particularly saline fluids—can dramatically reduce resistivity. Clay minerals, graphite, and metallic mineralization can also make rocks much more conductive.

rocks.mineral_composition: Primarily clay minerals (illite, smectite, kaolinite), quartz, feldspar and variable organic matter and carbonate minerals.
rocks.formation_env: Low-energy marine, lacustrine, deltaic or floodplain environments where fine-grained clay and silt accumulate and undergo compaction and lithification.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Generally low resistivity and relatively high conductivity compared with clean sandstone because of clay minerals and conductive pore fluids. Typically moderate-to-low density and low-to-moderate seismic velocity.

rocks.mineral_composition: Dominantly quartz with variable feldspar, lithic fragments, clay minerals and carbonate or silica cement.
rocks.formation_env: Fluvial, deltaic, aeolian, shallow-marine, coastal and submarine depositional environments.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Clean, dry sandstone is commonly highly resistive, whereas water-saturated sandstone can show much lower resistivity. Porosity and pore-fluid salinity strongly control electrical response. Common reservoir rock with strong acoustic and density-log response.

rocks.mineral_composition: Primarily calcite, with variable aragonite, dolomite, quartz, clay minerals and organic material.
rocks.formation_env: Marine carbonate platforms, shallow tropical seas, reefs, shelves, lagoons and carbonate mud environments.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Typically moderate-to-high resistivity when dense and dry. Fractured or water-filled limestone can become considerably more conductive. Relatively high density and seismic velocity compared with many clastic sediments.

rocks.mineral_composition: Dominantly dolomite mineral [CaMg(CO3)2], with variable calcite, quartz, clay and other carbonate minerals.
rocks.formation_env: Primarily shallow-marine carbonate platforms and restricted marine environments; commonly produced by dolomitization of limestone.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Generally relatively high resistivity and density. Porosity may be enhanced by dolomitization and dissolution, producing heterogeneous electrical and acoustic responses.

rocks.mineral_composition: Rounded gravel-sized clasts of quartzite, granite, limestone, sandstone and other rocks within a sand, silt or clay matrix and cement.
rocks.formation_env: High-energy fluvial channels, alluvial fans, braided rivers, beaches and conglomeratic deltaic environments.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Highly variable electrical and seismic properties because clast composition, matrix and pore-fluid content vary strongly. Often relatively resistive when clean and dry.

rocks.mineral_composition: Angular fragments of pre-existing rocks within a finer-grained matrix and cement; composition depends strongly on source rocks.
rocks.formation_env: Fault zones, talus slopes, debris flows, volcanic environments, collapse structures and high-energy sedimentary systems.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Strongly heterogeneous geophysical response. Fracture-related breccias may have high porosity and fluid conductivity, while well-cemented breccias can be dense and resistive.

rocks.mineral_composition: Clay minerals, quartz and feldspar with variable carbonate minerals, organic matter and iron oxides.
rocks.formation_env: Low-energy marine, lacustrine, floodplain and distal deltaic depositional environments.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Typically conductive and relatively low-resistivity because of clay minerals and pore fluids. Usually lower density and acoustic velocity than carbonate and crystalline basement rocks.

rocks.mineral_composition: Dominantly quartz and feldspar silt with variable clay minerals, mica, carbonate cement and lithic fragments.
rocks.formation_env: Floodplains, offshore shelves, distal deltas, lakes and other relatively low-energy depositional settings.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Intermediate electrical behavior between sandstone and shale. Clay content and pore-fluid salinity can significantly lower resistivity.

rocks.mineral_composition: Dominantly gypsum, CaSO4·2H2O, with variable anhydrite, halite, carbonate and clay impurities.
rocks.formation_env: Evaporitic basins, restricted marine lagoons, sabkhas, saline lakes and arid playa environments.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Relatively low density and potentially high resistivity when dry and pure. Hydration/dehydration and pore fluids strongly influence electrical and density properties.

rocks.mineral_composition: Dominantly halite, NaCl, with variable anhydrite, gypsum, sylvite, clay and other evaporite minerals.
rocks.formation_env: Large evaporitic marine basins, restricted seas, saline lakes and arid evaporite systems.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Very high resistivity when pure, dry and massive. Salt has low porosity and low electrical conductivity, making it a strong resistive body in electromagnetic and resistivity surveys. Salt diapirs can produce strong gravity and seismic velocity contrasts.

rocks.mineral_composition: Recrystallized calcite and/or dolomite with minor quartz, mica, graphite, pyrite and other accessory minerals.
rocks.formation_env: Forms by metamorphism of limestone or dolostone under elevated temperature and pressure, commonly in regional or contact metamorphic zones.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Generally dense and relatively resistive when dry and pure. Graphite, sulfides, fractures and fluids can substantially increase conductivity.

rocks.mineral_composition: Predominantly recrystallized quartz, commonly greater than 90 percent, with minor feldspar, mica and accessory minerals.
rocks.formation_env: Regional or contact metamorphism of quartz-rich sandstone under elevated temperature and pressure.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Very hard, dense and commonly highly resistive. Fracturing and fluid-filled joints can produce significant local conductivity.

rocks.mineral_composition: Very fine-grained quartz, mica, chlorite and clay-derived minerals, with variable feldspar and iron-bearing minerals.
rocks.formation_env: Low-grade regional metamorphism of shale or mudstone, typically in compressional tectonic environments.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Strongly anisotropic because of slaty cleavage. Electrical and seismic properties may vary substantially with measurement direction relative to foliation.

rocks.mineral_composition: Variable mixtures of mica, quartz, feldspar, chlorite, garnet, amphibole and other metamorphic minerals.
rocks.formation_env: Medium-grade regional metamorphism of shale, mudstone or other protoliths during mountain-building and crustal deformation.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Strong anisotropy caused by aligned mica and foliation. Graphite or sulfide-rich schists can be unusually conductive.

rocks.mineral_composition: Quartz, feldspar and mica with variable amphibole, pyroxene, garnet and other metamorphic minerals arranged in compositional bands.
rocks.formation_env: High-grade regional metamorphism of sedimentary or igneous protoliths at elevated temperature and pressure.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Generally dense, strong and resistive. Foliation produces seismic and electrical anisotropy. Mafic gneiss can be denser and more conductive than felsic gneiss.

rocks.mineral_composition: Quartz, alkali feldspar and plagioclase with variable biotite, muscovite, amphibole and accessory minerals.
rocks.formation_env: Slow crystallization of felsic magma deep within continental crust, commonly associated with continental arcs and mountain-building environments.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Generally high resistivity and moderate-to-high density. Fractures and groundwater can strongly reduce resistivity. Often forms resistive crystalline basement.

rocks.mineral_composition: Primarily plagioclase and pyroxene with variable olivine, magnetite and other mafic minerals.
rocks.formation_env: Rapid extrusion of mafic magma at oceanic ridges, hotspots, continental flood basalts and volcanic arcs.
rocks.geophysical_signature: High density and generally moderate-to-high resistivity when fresh and massive. Alteration and fluid-filled fractures can make basalt substantially more conductive. Strong magnetic response is common.

rocks.mineral_composition: Predominantly calcium-rich plagioclase and pyroxene with variable olivine, amphibole and iron-titanium oxides.
rocks.formation_env: Slow crystallization of mafic magma within the lower oceanic crust or shallow-to-deep intrusive bodies.
rocks.geophysical_signature: High density and generally resistive crystalline rock. Mafic mineral content can produce strong magnetic and gravity anomalies.

rocks.mineral_composition: Plagioclase feldspar with amphibole, biotite and minor pyroxene and quartz.
rocks.formation_env: Intermediate intrusive magma crystallizing slowly within continental crust, commonly associated with volcanic arcs and plutonic complexes.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Moderate-to-high density and generally high resistivity. Mafic mineral abundance influences magnetic susceptibility and density.

rocks.mineral_composition: Quartz, alkali feldspar and plagioclase with variable biotite, hornblende and volcanic glass.
rocks.formation_env: Rapid eruption of silica-rich magma in continental volcanic arcs, calderas and explosive volcanic systems.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Generally low-to-moderate density and high resistivity when fresh. Porous, fractured or hydrothermally altered rhyolite can have significantly lower resistivity.

rocks.mineral_composition: Mixture of carbonate minerals, principally calcite, with significant clay minerals and variable quartz and organic matter.
rocks.formation_env: Low-energy marine, lacustrine and shelf environments where carbonate mud and fine siliciclastic clay accumulate together.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Intermediate to relatively conductive behavior due to clay content and pore fluids. Density and resistivity generally lie between clean limestone and shale.

rocks.mineral_composition: Dominantly anhydrite, CaSO4, with variable gypsum, halite, dolomite, calcite and clay impurities.
rocks.formation_env: Evaporitic marine basins, sabkhas, restricted lagoons and sulfate-rich evaporite sequences; can also form by dehydration of gypsum.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Relatively high density and generally high resistivity when massive and dry. Often produces a strong density contrast with surrounding sedimentary rocks.

rocks.mineral_composition: Predominantly organic carbon-rich macerals derived from plant material, with variable moisture, mineral matter, clay, quartz, pyrite and carbonate minerals.
rocks.formation_env: Peat-forming wetlands and swamps followed by burial, compaction and coalification within sedimentary basins.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Low density relative to most sedimentary rocks and commonly relatively resistive, particularly when dry. Shale partings, moisture, pyrite and mineral matter can strongly alter the electrical response.

rocks.mineral_composition: Consolidated volcanic ash, glass shards and fragmented crystals or lithic particles; composition may be rhyolitic, dacitic, andesitic or basaltic.
rocks.formation_env: Explosive volcanic eruptions producing ash fall, pyroclastic flows and ash-rich volcanic deposits.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Highly variable density and resistivity due to vesicularity, welding, alteration and saturation. Welded tuff is denser and less porous than non-welded tuff. Hydrothermal alteration can strongly increase conductivity.

rocks.mineral_composition: Shaly (dirty) sandstone or thinly interbedded sand and shale: a mixed siliciclastic lithology containing variable quartz and feldspar from sandstone together with clay minerals and fine-grained matrix from shale.
rocks.formation_env: Fluvial, deltaic, coastal, shallow-marine and turbiditic environments where sand and mud are deposited in alternating beds or mixed facies.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Highly variable electrical response. Clean sandstone intervals can be resistive, while shale-rich intervals are substantially more conductive. Strong lithological contrasts commonly appear in well-log resistivity and gamma-ray data.

rocks.mineral_composition: Very pure, fine-grained low-magnesium calcite, commonly over 90 percent, built of coccolith plates and other calcareous nannofossils, with minor clay, quartz silt and chert (flint) nodules.
rocks.formation_env: Pelagic settling of calcareous nannofossil ooze in open marine shelf seas, most extensively in the Late Cretaceous to Paleocene; the North Sea Chalk Group (Tor and Ekofisk formations) is a major reservoir.
rocks.geophysical_signature: High porosity but low matrix permeability, so bulk density and sonic velocity drop sharply as porosity rises and increase with burial compaction. Water-saturated chalk is relatively conductive, hydrocarbon-bearing chalk markedly more resistive. Low gamma ray where clean; clay seams and chert layers stand out as log contrasts.

rocks.mineral_composition: Crystalline igneous and metamorphic rock beneath the sedimentary cover, typically granite, granodiorite, gneiss or schist, dominated by quartz, feldspar and mica with variable amphibole and other mafic minerals.
rocks.formation_env: Continental crust formed and deformed long before the overlying basin fill was deposited; on the Norwegian Continental Shelf commonly Caledonian or older granitic and metamorphic rock at the base of the sedimentary section.
rocks.geophysical_signature: Dense, fast and highly resistive where fresh, with a sharp step up in density, velocity and resistivity at the top-basement unconformity. Weathered or fractured basement can hold porosity and fluids, lowering resistivity and locally forming a reservoir.
